Results.ReviewText:
I bought this grill in 2017, and it has been the best grill I've ever owned!  I live in the PNW, and there is a lot of humidity, and rain.  I do keep the grill mostly covered when not in use, and it has held up very well against the elements!  

I just replaced the flavor bars this year because those had rusted, but that is pretty cheap and very easy to replace!  The cast iron grate is  perfect, all the features of the grill work perfect.    

The only sign of wear is a small rust spot on the stand below the hinge of the door which is superficial, and the red grill emblem on the knobs has faded a little. Otherwise, the grill looks just like when I got it!  

Very high quality, and I see many more years of fantastic grilling in our future!  I also love that I can fold down the wings when it isn't in use, and it doesn't take up my entire deck, very visually clean and attractive design.

Although not a "cheap" grill, it will save you a good amount of money vs cheap competitors!  My friend didn't like the price, and has had to buy a new $99 grill every year because they rust out and are unusable. I recommend this grill every person that has asked me about what kind of grill to get.

The grill is very expensive. The grill is relatively easy to assemble and  heats up quickly. A pleasure to use. The bottom hinge for the door is plastic and is already broken. I contacted Weber and the replacement hinge comes with the door hardware for over $15.

ClientResponses.Response:
We appreciate your feedback! We are sorry to hear that your new Spirit grill is not working properly but we are here to assist. Your grill should be able to reach the same high temperature we expect from all of our grills, at least 450 F. If your grill is not getting that hot, we would suggest double-checking the gas pressure from the LP tank. 

It sounds like your grill could be in "bypass" mode. Since the early 1990s, all regulators have included a safety device that restricts the flow of gas in the event of a gas leak. This safety device that we are speaking about, can be activated in two ways. The first way is to leave one or more burner control knobs in the "ON" position when the LP cylinder valve is opened. The second way is, not waiting long enough to "start" the grill after opening the LP cylinder valve. The safety device is activated each time the LP cylinder is opened. 

Here is a link we think might be helpful: 
https://consumer-care.weber.com/hc/en-us/articles/4977762826516-My-propane-gas-grill-isn-t-getting-very-hot-How-do-I-fix-this-

Thank you for bringing this to our attention, please lookout for an email from our Support team. We would like to hear more about this experience.
